en: Yes. She's pushing away everyone in her life but this man. She probably doesn't want to admit that what she's doing is wrong, even to herself.

But that is funny. Didn't your manager tell you?
Well, let's get right to it, shall we? So, what do you think about the Princess League system?
I mean, it must be great for unknown talent like you. You can get your face on TV, even without much proven experience.
Plus, the station can produce a profitable TV show without having to pay its talent very much. A win-win, right?
But, on the other hand, the level of talent is often hit-or-miss. Don't you think that lowers the overall quality of this type of program?
So taking all that into consideration, is the Princess League system really all that great?
The right to remain silent, huh? Well, that's all right. If I can't get a story out of you, we'll just have to put some other article in instead.
I mean, we don't want to bore our readers, right?
I think that's a question for the director. I'm just a contestant.

So, you don't care about the overall quality of the TV programming you benefit from? I see. Maybe the question was too difficult for you.
Well, the wonderful thing about the Princess League is that it gives girls a chance to compete, and truly try their very hardest at something worthwhile.

Ha. That sounds like a cop-out answer.

You know, with an attitude like that you'll never become anything more than mere decoration for the show.

I see. So you're basing your opinion on your own observations?

Yes. Somehow, the audience seems to get it right every time. I guess they're a pretty discerning bunch.

But in that case, wouldn't it follow that it doesn't matter if you win or lose because it's based on meaningless scores?
Hm. I guess that makes sense...
Haha. I guess it's a pretty flawed system, if even the contestants themselves don't believe in it. Wow, that'll sure get our reader's attention!
I think the scoring system is fair. Performances vary in quality, and I think the scores reflect that pretty accurately.
A performance can be technically skilled, but that isn't always what appeals to an audience.
Sometimes the value of a performance goes beyond technique, wouldn't you agree?
Of course. But the scores are the votes of each audience member, and I think they reflect how much the performer touched their heart individually.
So I don't believe the Princess League scores are based on technique alone.
You've got a point there. Hm. That's a pretty good answer, actually.
So that brings us to my last question. Now, to tell you the truth, I used to be a huge fan of a certain idol named Mirei Park.
Oh? You were Park-san's fan?
That's right. And I know you were her favorite. So, let me ask you this. Do you believe you will surpass her one day?
Hey, how am I supposed to make this into an interview if you won't even answer!?
This has been a complete waste of my time. Now I'll have to find some other article to put in place of your interview. Ugh, what a pain!
Come on, that was my best question!
Oh, well. I guess it really wasn't fair to ask you to answer a question like that.

Whoa! That's a bold statement! I didn't expect you to say something like that.

I see. Well, I certainly admire your spirit.
But that is quite a big boast, saying you've already surpassed Mirei Park.
I'll be following your career with an even more critical eye now.
I'm going to try my hardest to surpass her. Park-san is a personal idol of mine.
Good luck to you, then. From what I've seen, I think you just might be able to do it.
Oh! Do you really think so?
Are you surprised? Anyway, thank you for the great comment there at the end. That will really round out the article.
I don't think she and I can be compared. We each have our own individual paths. It's not about who surpasses whom.
I guess you have a point. But you know, as Park-san's favorite, I'll definitely be rooting for you.
You will?
